title: Minimum Spanning Repair

story.briefing: Every node must be reachable from every other, and each link costs what it costs. Reconnect the network for as little as possible.
story.success: Network reconnected at minimum cost. Nothing is isolated, nothing is wasted.

description:
A network is given as n nodes numbered 0 to n-1 and links [u, v, w], each an undirected connection between u and v costing w. Choose a set of links so that every node can reach every other, minimising the total cost. Return that total, or -1 if no such set exists. A single node needs no links and costs 0.

This level requires better than quadratic time in the number of links.

examples.explanation: Take the two cheapest; the third is redundant.

hints: Consider links from cheapest upward, taking each one unless it connects two nodes that are already connected to each other.
The whole difficulty is answering "are these two already connected?" quickly, thousands of times. Re-walking the network for each link is far too slow.

Sort the links by cost. Keep a union-find over the nodes; take a link only when its two endpoints have different roots, then merge them. Stop after taking n-1 links, and report -1 if you never reach that many.
